papers.title: Niche-driven divergence of prokaryotic and viral communities in Pogonatum cirratum.
papers.abstract: Ecological niche partitioning shapes microbial communities in terrestrial mosses, yet its underlying mechanisms and associated viral diversity remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized prokaryotic and viral communities in the rhizosphere soil (Rs) and endophytic niche (Pc) of Pogonatum cirratum using amplicon and metagenomic sequencing. Rs exhibited higher species richness, co-dominated by Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota, and Actinomycetota, whereas Pc was dominated by Pseudomonadota (81.13%) but showed greater functional diversity. Source tracking revealed that 10.57% of Pc taxa origin
papers.summary: This study characterizes the prokaryotic and viral communities in the rhizosphere soil and endophytic niche of the moss Pogonatum cirratum, revealing distinct niche-driven divergence in species richness, composition, and functional diversity. The endophytic niche is dominated by Pseudomonadota but shows greater functional diversity, and source tracking indicates limited microbial migration from soil, highlighting the unique selective pressures of the moss endosphere.

papers.title: Prospective associations of tea consumption with skeletal muscle mass and strength: Insights from the gut microbiome and proteomics.
papers.abstract: Tea consumption may be associated with skeletal muscle health, but longitudinal evidence based on repeated assessments remains limited. We examined the associations of tea intake and serum biomarkers with repeated skeletal muscle measures and explored whether these associations might be partly explained by multi-omics features. In this prospective cohort, 3408 adults were followed for approximately 12 years. Skeletal muscle mass was measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, handgrip strength by digital dynamometry, gut microbial taxonomic and functional profiles by shotgun metagenomic sequ
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of 3,408 adults over 12 years found that tea consumption is associated with better skeletal muscle mass and strength, and suggests that gut microbiome composition and serum proteomics may partly mediate these benefits. The findings provide longitudinal evidence linking tea intake to muscle health and highlight potential multi-omics mechanisms.

papers.title: Comparative effects of mannanoligosaccharides, fructooligosaccharides, and potato resistant starch on intestinal integrity, antioxidant status, and cecal microbiota in commercial laying hens.
papers.abstract: Functional carbohydrates are increasingly used as alternatives to antibiotic growth promoters because of their ability to modulate intestinal health and microbial populations. However, comparative information regarding the effects of structurally different prebiotic compounds in laying hens remains limited. This study aimed to compare the effects of mannanoligosaccharides (MOS), fructooligosaccharides (FOS), and potato resistant starch (RS) on productive performance, intestinal integrity, antioxidant status, intestinal morphology, and cecal microbiota in commercial laying hens.
papers.summary: This study compares the effects of three prebiotics—mannanoligosaccharides, fructooligosaccharides, and potato resistant starch—on intestinal health, antioxidant status, and cecal microbiota in laying hens. The findings provide comparative data on how structurally different prebiotics influence gut integrity and microbial communities, which is relevant for optimizing poultry nutrition.

papers.title: Distinct gut microbiome profiles characterize obese and non-obese patients with atherosclerosis: a metagenomic analysis.
papers.abstract: Obesity is widely recognized as an aggravating risk factor for atherosclerosis (AS), yet the effects of obesity on AS-associated microbiome dysbiosis are not sufficiently characterized. This study aims to identify the contribution of obesity-related dysbiosis in AS.
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic analysis to compare gut microbiome profiles between obese and non-obese patients with atherosclerosis, revealing distinct microbial signatures associated with obesity. The findings suggest that obesity contributes to specific gut microbiome dysbiosis in atherosclerosis, potentially informing more personalized therapeutic approaches.

papers.title: Microbial metabolite-driven mechanisms linking the gut microbiome to atherosclerosis: multi-omic and translational perspectives.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and a substantial residual risk persists despite optimal management of traditional risk factors. Increasing evidence implicates the gut microbiome as a mechanistic contributor to atherogenesis, not merely through taxonomic shifts but via the production of bioactive microbial metabolites that link diet, microbial metabolism, and host vascular biology. These metabolites have emerged as central effectors of the gut-artery axis, influencing intestinal barrier integrity, systemic immunity, lipid handling, and t
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current evidence on how gut microbiome-derived metabolites contribute to atherosclerosis, highlighting the gut-artery axis and its effects on intestinal barrier function, immunity, and lipid metabolism. It emphasizes multi-omic approaches and translational perspectives to link microbial metabolism with cardiovascular disease risk.

papers.title: Gut microbiome signatures during acute infection are associated with long COVID.
papers.abstract: Long COVID (LC) manifests in 10%-30% of non-hospitalized individuals post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, leading to significant morbidity. The predictive role of gut microbiome composition during acute infection in the development of LC is not well understood, partly because of the heterogeneous nature of the disease.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether gut microbiome composition during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection can predict the development of long COVID. The findings suggest that specific gut microbiome signatures are associated with long COVID, potentially offering early biomarkers for risk assessment.

papers.title: Environmental selection shapes the ecological cascade of biofilm assembly and functional gene abundance in sandstone weathering.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms are pivotal agents in the process of sandstone weathering; nevertheless, the ecological mechanisms that govern their transition from mere colonization to sustained weathering activity remain ambiguous. This study systematically elucidated microbe-mediated weathering mechanisms through amplicon and metagenomic sequencing of bacteria, fungi, and archaea across a sandstone weathering sequence-from original unweathered sandstone (OS), biofilm-covered sandstone (BS), to weathered sandstone (WS). The findings indicate that microbial communities undergo associations across a weathering
papers.summary: This study uses amplicon and metagenomic sequencing to show that as sandstone weathers, microbial communities shift from simple colonization to active weathering, with environmental selection driving the assembly of biofilms and the abundance of functional genes involved in mineral degradation.

papers.title: Deployable high-fidelity metagenome binning at scale with QuickBin.
papers.abstract: Reconstructing genomes from metagenomic assemblies is foundational to microbiome research, yet binning faces a persistent trade-off between fidelity and throughput. Many high-accuracy methods rely on GPU-intensive workflows, marker-gene postprocessing, or heavy computational resources, limiting reproducible use at scale. Here, we present QuickBin, a CPU-native, marker-free binning algorithm designed to recover near-complete, ultra-low-contamination metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) efficiently. QuickBin pairs a GC-coverage spatial index (BinMap) with an early-exit Oracle cascade of similarit
papers.summary: QuickBin is a new CPU-native, marker-free metagenome binning algorithm that recovers near-complete, ultra-low-contamination genomes efficiently at scale, addressing the trade-off between fidelity and throughput. It uses a GC-coverage spatial index (BinMap) and an early-exit Oracle cascade to achieve high accuracy without GPU-intensive workflows, making it suitable for reproducible large-scale microbiome studies.

papers.title: Improving Dietary Data Quality in Nutrition Studies: Development and Validation of an Explainable, Reproducible, Open Machine Learning-Assisted Framework for Outlier Detection in 24-Hour Recalls.
papers.abstract: Twenty-four-hour dietary recalls (24HRs) are widely used in nutritional epidemiology, but repeated administration is required to capture within-person variability, introducing temporal dependence and challenges for data cleaning. Existing outlier detection approaches are largely static, manual, and based on adult-centric thresholds, limiting reproducibility and scalability. We developed and validated an explainable, reproducible machine learning (ML)-assisted framework to detect and evaluate implausible intake values in cross-sectional and longitudinal 24HRs and to generate AI-ready dietary da
papers.summary: This paper presents a new machine learning-assisted framework for detecting implausible values in 24-hour dietary recall data, addressing limitations of existing static and manual methods. The framework is explainable, reproducible, and open, and it is designed to handle both cross-sectional and longitudinal data, ultimately producing AI-ready dietary datasets for further research.

papers.title: Large language models enhance annotation of enzymes in metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic data have notable biological potential, but their functional interpretation is frequently impeded by incomplete protein function annotations. Accurate enzyme annotation is essential for elucidating the metabolic capabilities of microbial communities within metagenomic datasets. To address this challenge, we developed FEDKEA, an enzyme annotation tool leveraging protein language models, and provided a web platform for its use. In addition, we designed a user-friendly, FEDKEA-based metagenomic pipeline, MEnzMap, which encompasses the entire analysis workflow-from raw data quality con
papers.summary: The authors developed FEDKEA, an enzyme annotation tool that uses protein language models to improve functional annotation of metagenomic data, along with a web platform and a user-friendly pipeline called MEnzMap that covers the full analysis workflow from raw data to enzyme mapping. This addresses the common problem of incomplete protein function annotations in metagenomes, enabling better elucidation of microbial metabolic capabilities.

papers.title: The gut microbiome organ.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome is increasingly viewed as an active regulator of host physiology, extending beyond earlier taxonomy-centered descriptions of a complex microbial community. Accumulating evidence supports an organ-like conceptual framework in which the gut microbiome exhibits spatially structured organization, extensive metabolic capacity, and continuous bidirectional communication with host systems. Through the production of bioactive metabolites with endocrine-like, immunomodulatory, and neuromodulatory properties, the microbiome contributes to metabolic, immune, and neuroendocrine re
papers.summary: This paper proposes a conceptual framework for viewing the human gut microbiome as an organ, highlighting its spatially structured organization, metabolic capacity, and bidirectional communication with the host. It emphasizes the microbiome's role in producing bioactive metabolites that influence metabolic, immune, and neuroendocrine functions, supporting a shift from taxonomy-based descriptions to a functional, organ-like perspective.

papers.title: Mapping the causal landscape of polycystic ovary syndrome: A systematic Mendelian randomization evidence synthesis and the MR-PCOS atlas platform.
papers.abstract: Mendelian randomization (MR) studies have increasingly investigated potential predicted antecedents and consequences of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), yet published evidence remains scattered across diverse exposures, outcomes, and analytical frameworks. This study aimed to systematically organize published PCOS-related MR evidence and develop an interactive platform to support evidence retrieval, comparison, and interpretation. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to June 1, 2026. Original MR Studies were eligible if PCOS was either the exposu
papers.summary: This paper systematically reviews published Mendelian randomization studies on polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and creates an interactive atlas platform to organize and interpret the scattered evidence. It provides a comprehensive synthesis of causal relationships between various exposures/outcomes and PCOS, serving as a valuable resource for researchers.

papers.title: Exploration of the mechanism of gut microbiota-mediated immune modulation in the pathogenesis of pancreatic cancer: A Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of pancreatic cancer is complex. While immune dysregulation and gut microbiota disturbances are considered key factors, the causal pathway between them remains unclear. This study employs a 2-step Mendelian randomization (MR) approach to empirically investigate the "immune cells - gut microbiota - pancreatic cancer" mediation pathway from a genetic perspective. Relevant data on 731 immune cell phenotypes (N = 3757), 473 gut microbiota (N=8293), and pancreatic cancer (N = 3,87,888) were extracted from large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) and FinnGen summary statisti
papers.summary: This study uses a two-step Mendelian randomization approach to investigate whether gut microbiota influence pancreatic cancer risk through immune cell modulation. The authors identify specific microbial taxa and immune cell phenotypes that may mediate this pathway, providing genetic evidence for a causal chain linking the gut microbiome, immune system, and pancreatic cancer.

papers.title: Gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and allergic diseases: A bidirectional Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Some authors suggest a link between gut microbiota and allergic diseases; however, the genetically predicted relationship and the role of inflammatory proteins as mediators are still uncertain. Gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 5 types of allergic diseases, namely allergic rhinitis (AR), atopic dermatitis, allergic conjunctivitis, food allergy, and asthma, were identified from large-scale genome-wide association studies summary data. In a 2-sample, bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) study, we systematically conducted 2980 primary tests (298 exposures tested bidirectionally aga
papers.summary: This study uses bidirectional Mendelian randomization to investigate causal links between gut microbiota and five allergic diseases, finding that certain microbial taxa may influence allergy risk, with inflammatory proteins potentially mediating these effects. The results support a role for the gut microbiome in allergic disease pathogenesis, though the effects are modest and require further validation.

papers.title: A noninvasive 13C-mannitol breath test to monitor semaglutide treatment-induced delayed oral-cecal transit in mice.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), such as semaglutide, are highly effective treatments for obesity and type 2 diabetes but are often associated with gastrointestinal side effects including delayed transit times through the gastrointestinal tract. We present a non-invasive breath test to measure oral-cecal transit time (OCTT) in mice that could be readily translated to clinical studies. Current methods for measuring OCTT are limited by invasiveness, terminal procedures, anesthesia, radioactive tracers, or stress-induced influence on the outcomes. Here we demonstrate that 13C
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
papers.summary: This paper introduces a noninvasive 13C-mannitol breath test to measure oral-cecal transit time in mice, demonstrating its ability to monitor delayed gastrointestinal transit caused by semaglutide treatment. The method avoids invasive procedures, anesthesia, and radioactive tracers, and is potentially translatable to clinical studies.

papers.title: Age-adjusted machine learning identifies facial skin microbes associated with skin quality among Korean women.
papers.abstract: Recognizing specific microbes that significantly influence skin quality is becoming an essential aspect of personalized skincare. However, conventional large-scale cohort skin microbiome studies often overlook important confounders, such as age, leading to missing meaningful microbe-skin relationships. In this study, we developed an age-adjusted machine learning (AAML) framework to identify microbial candidates associated with skin quality by determining optimal age ranges that enhance age-independent signals of skin microbes. It allowed the identification of distinct age groups that clearly e
papers.summary: This study developed an age-adjusted machine learning framework to identify facial skin microbes associated with skin quality in Korean women, overcoming the confounding effect of age. By determining optimal age ranges, the framework revealed distinct microbial candidates linked to skin quality that conventional analyses might miss.

papers.title: Multi-omics identifies microbial and miRNA biomarkers from rumen fluid for susceptibility of subacute ruminal acidosis in dairy goats.
papers.abstract: With the increasing intensification of animal husbandry, high-concentrate diets are often used in production to ensure high production performance in dairy animals, leading to susceptibility to subacute rumen acidosis (SARA), yet reliable early diagnostic biomarkers remain lacking. In this study, a high-RDS diet was fed to dairy goats as a model, and SARA-tolerant and SARA-susceptible individuals were identified under this diet. By combining 16S rRNA gene sequencing, metagenomic binning, and miRNA transcriptome sequencing, the changes in rumen microbial composition, function, and miRNAs in dai
papers.summary: This study identifies microbial and miRNA biomarkers in rumen fluid that distinguish dairy goats susceptible to subacute ruminal acidosis (SARA) from tolerant ones, using multi-omics approaches including 16S rRNA sequencing, metagenomic binning, and miRNA transcriptomics. The findings provide potential early diagnostic markers for SARA, which could improve management of high-concentrate diets in dairy animals.

papers.title: Microbiome modelling for post-mortem interval estimation across species and climates: swine analogues in a British summer and external validation in human donors from the USA.
papers.abstract: Background Microbial clocks have shown high accuracy in estimating time since death, or post-mortem interval (PMI), across diverse contexts, including controlled laboratory settings, outdoor environments, and both human cadavers and animal models. However, the limited number of studies performed under different environmental and climatic conditions, particularly in Europe, restricts the broader applicability of these models, as data from distinct climates may not reliably translate across geographic regions. This study investigates the nasal thanatomicrobiome of pig carcasses exposed to outdoo
papers.summary: This study evaluates the use of nasal microbiome 'clocks' to estimate post-mortem interval (PMI) in pig carcasses exposed to a British summer, and tests whether models trained on these swine data can be applied to human donor samples from the USA. The findings highlight the challenges of cross-species and cross-climate generalization, emphasizing the need for region- and species-specific models for accurate PMI estimation.

papers.title: AI-guided computational design of synthetic microbiota for next-generation immunomodulatory applications.
papers.abstract: The growing recognition of the human microbiome as a key regulator of immune homeostasis has accelerated the application of computational intelligence for microbiome-driven disease understanding and therapeutic design. However, existing microbiome studies largely rely on classical machine learning or shallow deep learning models that fail to capture higher-order microbial interactions, multimodal functional dependencies, and immune feasibility constraints simultaneously. Moreover, most approaches lack biological constraint enforcement, leading to predictions that may be statistically accurate
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of AI-guided computational design for synthetic microbiota in immunomodulatory applications, highlighting the limitations of current machine learning and deep learning models in capturing complex microbial interactions and enforcing biological constraints. It emphasizes the need for more advanced computational approaches to design effective microbiome-based therapies.

papers.title: A Diffusion-Driven CH4-O2 Boundary Structures Methane Oxidation and Carbon Transformation in Upland Soils.
papers.abstract: Although extensive work has characterized high-affinity atmospheric methane oxidation in upland soils and sustained oxidation in chronically methane-rich environments, shallow point-source inputs introduce transient methane pulses into otherwise aerated heterotrophic soils. Whether these pulses migrate rapidly toward the atmosphere or instead create localized redox boundaries that restructure soil carbon pools and microbial metabolism remains unclear. Here, we conducted a controlled natural gas release experiment to quantify coupled geochemical and microbial responses in near-surface soils acr
papers.summary: This study investigates how transient methane pulses in upland soils create localized redox boundaries that influence methane oxidation and carbon transformation. Using a controlled natural gas release experiment, the authors quantify coupled geochemical and microbial responses, revealing that diffusion-driven CH4-O2 boundaries structure microbial metabolism and soil carbon pools.

papers.title: Identification of a Novel Fungal α‑l‑Fucosidase with Transfucosylation Potential.
papers.abstract: Fucosylated carbohydrates are a vital part of human nutrition. They act as prebiotics, nourishing beneficial gut bacteria and helping shape the gut microbiome. Enzymatic synthesis is a convenient method to access these molecules. Fungal α-l-fucosidases are glycoside hydrolases that naturally cleave terminal α-linked fucose residues from glycans; those with synthetic capabilities are conveniently applicable in glycoengineering. This study investigates the fucosylation potential and regioselectivity of rare GH29 α-l-fucosidases from filamentous fungi. The screening of production of putative α-l-
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes a novel fungal α-l-fucosidase from the GH29 family that can both cleave and synthesize fucosylated carbohydrates, with potential for glycoengineering. The enzyme shows transfucosylation activity, enabling the synthesis of fucosylated prebiotics that may benefit gut health.

papers.title: Promises and Pitfalls of Long-Read Sequencing for Resolving Microbial Complexity.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing (LRS) has driven a transition in microbial genomics, overcoming the assembly fragmentation inherent to short-read sequencing. This review elucidates the impact of LRS across isolate genomics, metagenomics, and multi-omics domains. By spanning extensive repetitive regions, LRS facilitates the reconstruction of circular chromosomes and precisely resolves mobile genetic elements (MGEs). In metagenomics, LRS enables strain-level resolution, the recovery of circular metagenome-assembled genomes, and the precise localization of MGEs within host replicons. Furthermore, the single
papers.summary: This review discusses how long-read sequencing has transformed microbial genomics by overcoming assembly fragmentation, enabling complete circular genomes and precise resolution of mobile genetic elements. It also highlights applications in metagenomics for strain-level resolution and multi-omics integration, while noting current limitations and challenges.

papers.title: How Gut Microbiota Influence Healthy Aging: Overview of Reviews.
papers.abstract: Background: Gut microbiota plays a key role in the aging process, with age-related microbial shifts contributing to chronic inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, frailty, and cognitive decline. Despite growing interest, an integrated synthesis of how diet and lifestyle modifications influence gut microbiota remains limited. This overview of reviews summarizes the current evidence on how dietary and lifestyle interventions shape microbial composition and affect aging outcomes. Methods: Following the PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed and Scopus for English-language reviews (January 2023-Octob
papers.summary: This overview of reviews synthesizes current evidence on how dietary and lifestyle interventions shape gut microbiota composition and influence healthy aging outcomes, including inflammation, metabolic function, frailty, and cognition. It highlights that while specific interventions show promise, integrated synthesis is still limited, underscoring the need for more comprehensive research.

papers.title: Environmental filtering shapes biosynthetic potential and resistome of antarctic microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Environmental filtering is a major driver of microbial community assembly in Antarctic ecosystems, yet its influence on biosynthetic potential and antimicrobial resistance remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed 319 medium- to high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) recovered from four Antarctic sites (Whalers Bay, Crater Lake, Fumarole Bay, and Hannah Point) to investigate the relationship between geochemical gradients, biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). Integrating genome-resolved metagenomics, biosynthetic mining, resistome profiling,
papers.summary: This study analyzed 319 metagenome-assembled genomes from four Antarctic sites to show that environmental filtering, driven by geochemical gradients, shapes both the biosynthetic potential (BGCs) and antimicrobial resistance (ARGs) of microbial communities. The findings reveal that specific environmental conditions select for distinct biosynthetic and resistance traits, providing insights into natural product discovery and antibiotic resistance in extreme environments.

papers.title: Sodium Butyrate Therapy in Ulcerative Colitis: A Systematic Review of Preclinical and Clinical Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sodium butyrate, a short-chain fatty acid produced by gut microbial fermentation of dietary fiber, has attracted increasing interest as a potential adjunctive therapy for ulcerative colitis (UC) because of its anti-inflammatory, barrier-protective, and immunomodulatory properties. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the current clinical and preclinical evidence regarding the efficacy and mechanisms of sodium butyrate in UC. Methods: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261437741). PubMed/ME
papers.summary: This systematic review evaluates the evidence for sodium butyrate as a therapy for ulcerative colitis, summarizing its anti-inflammatory, barrier-protective, and immunomodulatory effects from preclinical and clinical studies. The findings support its potential as an adjunctive treatment, though the authors highlight the need for more robust clinical trials to confirm efficacy and optimal dosing.

papers.title: AI-guided discovery of antimicrobial peptides for urinary tract infections leveraging a new catalogue of the human urinary microbiome.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are common infections that pose a critical burden on healthcare and society. Despite growing recognition that the human urinary tract harbors its own microbiome, its composition, functional potential, and alterations in UTI remain limited. Here, we leveraged the publicly available whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing data from 450 urinary microbiome samples collected in four independent cohorts together with genome assembly and metagenomic binning to construct an extensive human urinary microbiome catalog consisting of ∼1.3 million non-redundant microbial genes a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint constructs a comprehensive catalog of the human urinary microbiome from 450 metagenomic samples, comprising ~1.3 million non-redundant genes, and uses AI-guided discovery to identify antimicrobial peptides with potential for treating urinary tract infections. The work provides a new resource for understanding the urinary microbiome and demonstrates a computational approach for peptide-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Robust and Interpretable Metagenomic Modeling Through Structure-Aware Multi-View Learning and Attribution-Guided Biological Insight.
papers.abstract: Integrative modeling of metagenomic and clinical data can advance the study of host phenotypes, but remains challenged by cross-view heterogeneity, uncertain generalizability, and poor interpretability. We developed SAMECAT (Structure-Aware Metagenomics multi-viEw Contrastive AlignmenT), a structure-aware deep learning framework that integrates species-level shotgun metagenomic profiles with mixed-type clinical covariates through view-specific encoders, clustering-informed contrastive alignment, and adaptive representation fusion. Using two independent Louisiana Osteoporosis Study datasets gen
papers.summary: SAMECAT is a new deep learning framework that integrates metagenomic and clinical data using structure-aware multi-view learning and contrastive alignment, improving robustness and interpretability. Applied to two independent osteoporosis cohorts, it demonstrates better generalizability and provides attribution-guided biological insights into host phenotypes.

papers.title: Emergent function, not microbial conformity: functional redundancy and the limits of taxonomic inference in microbiome genomics.
papers.abstract: Microbiome genomics has achieved remarkable resolution of community structure, yet composition alone remains an unstable basis for inferring host-relevant biology. That instability reflects a broader interpretive problem in which taxonomically distinct communities can converge on similar outputs, while superficially similar communities can diverge in behaviour because of strain variation, gene content, regulatory state, ecological context, spatial organization and host physiology. Functional redundancy is therefore better understood not as a reserve of interchangeable organisms but as a distri
papers.summary: This paper argues that taxonomic composition is an unreliable proxy for microbiome function, because functionally redundant communities can be taxonomically distinct and vice versa. It proposes that functional redundancy should be viewed as a distributed property shaped by strain variation, gene content, and ecological context, rather than as interchangeable organisms.

papers.title: theBIGbam: compression and interactive exploration of large-scale sequencing alignments with circular mapping support.
papers.abstract: theBIGbam (github.com/bhagavadgitadu22/theBIGbam) is a genome browser and alignment viewer designed for massive metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets. The tool takes BAM files containing read alignments, together with genome assemblies in FASTA format or annotated genome sequences in GenBank format. Alternatively, it can start from raw FASTQ reads and generate alignments using a modified mapper that supports circular genomes, enabling seamless read mapping across genome ends. theBIGbam can compress hundreds of gigabytes of input files 10- to 100-fold into dedicated databases while retain
papers.summary: theBIGbam is a new genome browser and alignment viewer tailored for massive metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets. It compresses BAM/FASTQ data 10- to 100-fold into dedicated databases and supports circular genome mapping, enabling efficient interactive exploration of large-scale sequencing alignments.

papers.title: ViralQC: a tool for assessing completeness and contamination of predicted viral contigs.
papers.abstract: Viruses represent the most abundant biological entities on Earth, playing vital roles in diverse ecosystems. Cataloging viruses across various environments is essential for understanding their properties and functions. Metagenomic sequencing has emerged as the most comprehensive method for virus discovery. However, distinguishing viral sequences from the vast background of microbial organisms in metagenomic data remains a significant challenge. Existing tools experience varying degrees of false positive rates due to noise in sequencing and assembly, and the integration of proviruses into micro
papers.summary: ViralQC is a new tool that assesses the completeness and contamination of predicted viral contigs from metagenomic data, addressing the challenge of false positives in virus discovery. It helps researchers distinguish true viral sequences from noise and microbial contamination, improving the reliability of viral cataloging.

papers.title: Immune Cell-Mediated Causal Link Between Gut Microbiota Traits and Childhood Asthma: Evidence From Mendelian Randomization and Metagenomic Sequencing.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota may be involved in childhood asthma. However, the causal relationship between the gut microbiota and childhood asthma remains obscure. Whether immune cells mediate the pathway from gut microbiota to childhood asthma has not been elucidated.
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and metagenomic sequencing to investigate the causal relationship between gut microbiota traits and childhood asthma, finding evidence that certain gut microbes influence asthma risk and that immune cells may mediate this pathway.

papers.title: Optimized Controlled-Release Fertilization Improves Productivity and Reshapes the Rhizosphere Microbiome in Lei Bamboo: A Metagenomic Assessment.
papers.abstract: Intensive nitrogen fertilization in Lei bamboo (Phyllostachys praecox) plantations has increased productivity but has also reduced nitrogen-use efficiency (NUE), accelerated nutrient losses, and contributed to soil degradation. How nutrient-release strategies influence rhizosphere microbiome assembly and ecosystem functioning remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a bamboo shoot-specific controlled-release fertilizer (CRF) and evaluated different urea-CRF blending ratios to identify sustainable fertilization strategy for Lei bamboo production. Mixed CRF-urea treatments outperformed both
papers.summary: This study developed a controlled-release fertilizer (CRF) for Lei bamboo and tested different blending ratios with urea, finding that mixed CRF-urea treatments improved productivity and reshaped the rhizosphere microbiome compared to conventional fertilization. Metagenomic analysis revealed that optimized fertilization enhanced nitrogen-use efficiency and promoted beneficial microbial functions, offering a more sustainable fertilization strategy for bamboo plantations.

papers.title: The Gut Mycobiome in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Reframing Candida as a Signal of Ecosystem Disruption.
papers.abstract: Growing interest in the gut mycobiome has renewed focus on Candida spp. in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Yet, fecal detection remains difficult to interpret, given its uncertain relationship with intestinal inflammation. This narrative review synthesizes historical, mechanistic, observational, and interventional evidence to distinguish colonization, relative abundance, mucosal invasion, virulence transitions, and potential contributions to IBD.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the role of the gut mycobiome, particularly Candida species, in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). It synthesizes evidence to argue that fecal Candida detection should be interpreted as a marker of ecosystem disruption rather than a direct cause of inflammation, distinguishing between colonization, relative abundance, and mucosal invasion.

papers.title: Bioactive Components and Functional Applications of Sea Buckthorn: A Review.
papers.abstract: Sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.) is a medicinal and edible plant rich in polyphenols, vitamins, fatty acids, carotenoids, and polysaccharides. These constituents are associated with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, gut microbiota-modulating, antibacterial, and other health-related activities, supporting its potential use in functional foods, nutraceuticals, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics. However, its composition and bioactivity vary with plant part, extract type, and processing method, which complicates comparison across studies. This review evaluates sea buckthorn as
papers.summary: This review summarizes the bioactive components of sea buckthorn, including polyphenols, vitamins, fatty acids, carotenoids, and polysaccharides, and their associated health benefits such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and gut microbiota-modulating activities. It highlights the variability in composition and bioactivity depending on plant part, extract type, and processing method, which complicates cross-study comparisons. The paper supports the potential use of sea buckthorn in functional foods, nutraceuticals, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics.

papers.title: The multi-omics fallacy in microbiome science.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence and machine-learning-assisted multi-omics have expanded the scale and ambition of microbiome research, but they have also sharpened an older interpretive problem. Biologically plausible structure is too easily mistaken for biological explanation. This Perspective defines the multi-omics fallacy as claim inflation that occurs when integrating microbial, host, environmental, spatial, and clinical data is assumed to move interpretation from association toward verified mechanism without a corresponding gain in measurement, localization, temporal resolution, functional linka
papers.summary: This Perspective article defines the 'multi-omics fallacy' in microbiome research, where integrating diverse omics data is mistakenly assumed to automatically yield mechanistic insights. The authors argue that biologically plausible correlations are often overinterpreted as causal explanations without adequate experimental validation, and they call for more rigorous approaches to bridge association and mechanism.

papers.title: MAAMOUL: metabolic network-based discovery of microbiome-metabolome shifts in disease.
papers.abstract: A central goal in human gut microbiome research is to identify disease-associated functional shifts, an objective increasingly pursued through metagenomic and metabolomic assays. However, common differential abundance analyses of genes or metabolites often yield long and difficult-to-interpret feature lists. Aggregating features into predefined pathways can improve interpretability but relies on fixed pathway boundaries that may not reflect context-specific functional changes. Moreover, even when paired metagenomic-metabolomic data are available, they are often analyzed separately or linked on
papers.summary: MAAMOUL is a new computational tool that integrates paired metagenomic and metabolomic data using metabolic network models to identify disease-associated functional shifts in the gut microbiome. By aggregating features into context-specific metabolic modules rather than fixed pathways, it improves interpretability and reveals coordinated changes across genes and metabolites.

papers.title: Maternal and Infant Skin Microbiome Synchrony and Divergence: A Longitudinal Study of Skin Microbial Ecology and Early-Life Assembly.
papers.abstract: During pregnancy and after childbirth, women's skin undergoes significant changes which may affect the skin's functional and structural characteristics and microbial diversity. Like their mothers, the newborns also experience various skin challenges in the months following birth. Temporal changes in skin microbiome in special groups such as pregnant women and newborns, as well as the interrelation between their skin's microbial diversity, have not been investigated. We followed women from pregnancy through 6 months after delivery, and their infants from 4 weeks to 6 months of age to investigat
papers.summary: This longitudinal study tracked the skin microbiomes of mothers from pregnancy through 6 months postpartum and their infants from 4 weeks to 6 months of age, revealing both synchrony and divergence in microbial diversity and composition between maternal and infant skin over time. The findings highlight dynamic microbial assembly in early life and its relationship to maternal skin changes, providing new insights into mother-infant microbiome transmission and development.

papers.title: Genome-resolved insights into hydrocarbon-transforming and nitrate-reducing microbial communities from deep petroleum reservoir cores of the Nashpa Oil Field, Pakistan.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities from deep subsurface petroleum reservoirs are adapted to hydrocarbon-rich, oxygen-limited, and physicochemically extreme environments. However, genome-resolved knowledge of petroleum reservoir microbiomes from Pakistan remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study provides the first genome-resolved analysis of microbial communities in deep petroleum reservoir cores from Pakistan's Nashpa Oil Field, revealing hydrocarbon-transforming and nitrate-reducing microorganisms. The findings expand our understanding of subsurface microbial diversity and metabolic potential in extreme, hydrocarbon-rich environments.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into microbial communities of terrestrial mud volcanos: functional diversity of subsurface archaea and bacteria.
papers.abstract: Terrestrial mud volcanoes are surface geological features where fluidized sediments and gasses from the subsurface are discharged along a fracture network providing a window into the deep biosphere. Although mud volcanoes constitute an important source of methane emission from natural environments, their microbial communities responsible for methane cycling remain poorly characterized. Using a metagenomics approach, we investigated the taxonomic composition and metabolic potential of microbial communities in three active mud volcanoes in the Kerch-Taman mud volcanic province. Despite the volca
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to characterize the microbial communities in three terrestrial mud volcanoes in the Kerch-Taman province, revealing their taxonomic composition and metabolic potential, particularly for methane cycling. The findings provide new insights into the functional diversity of subsurface archaea and bacteria in these deep biosphere windows.

papers.title: Wastewater treatment plant effluent alters particle-associated bacterial assemblages in an intermittent stream.
papers.abstract: Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTPs) can be point-sources of nutrients, organic matter, anthropogenic contaminants, and microbes to lotic environments, and the input of WWTP effluent can alter the activity and composition of stream microbial assemblages in the benthos and water column. Within the stream benthos, fine particulate matter (FPM) supports especially high levels of microbial activity, but the effect of WWTP effluents on the microbial communities specifically associated with benthic FPM in rivers has not been studied. The present work sought to address this knowledge gap by analyzing
papers.summary: This study investigates how wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) effluent affects microbial communities attached to fine particulate matter (FPM) in the benthos of an intermittent stream. The findings reveal that effluent input significantly alters the composition of particle-associated bacterial assemblages, highlighting a previously understudied impact of WWTP discharge on stream ecosystems.

papers.title: PUDU (pipeline for universal diversity unveiling): an accessible end-to-end workflow for taxonomic profiling and ecological visualization of environmental microbiomes across amplicon, shotgun, and long-read sequencing.
papers.abstract: Environmental microbiome research has advanced through three complementary sequencing modalities, targeted 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, whole-genome shotgun (WGS) metagenomics, and long-read full-length 16S rRNA profiling, each supported by distinct toolsets with heterogeneous outputs, variable configurations, and different levels of reproducibility documentation. Existing pipelines are typically modality-specific, require substantial configuration expertise, or produce outputs that need further custom scripting before standard ecological analyses can begin. This analytical fragmentation intr
papers.summary: PUDU is a new end-to-end bioinformatics pipeline that unifies taxonomic profiling and ecological visualization for environmental microbiomes across amplicon, shotgun, and long-read sequencing data. It addresses the fragmentation of existing modality-specific tools by providing an accessible, reproducible workflow that generates outputs ready for standard ecological analyses without extensive custom scripting.

papers.title: Metagenomic Characterization of Nitrite-Negative Urinary Tract Infections and Identification of an optrA-fexA Co-Localization in a Primary Healthcare Setting in China.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) showing negative nitrite results create a diagnostic blind spot for Gram-positive pathogens. The plasmid-mediated resistance genes optrA (linezolid) and tet(X) (tigecycline) pose severe therapeutic challenges, but their genomic context in primary healthcare settings remains poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the microbial community in nitrite-negative urinary tract infections (UTIs), revealing a diagnostic blind spot for Gram-positive pathogens. It also identifies a plasmid co-localizing the antibiotic resistance genes optrA (linezolid) and fexA (chloramphenicol/florfenicol) in a primary healthcare setting in China, highlighting a genomic context that could facilitate the spread of resistance.

papers.title: Cross sectional analysis of gut microbiota of ALS patients with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study investigated the differences in gut microbiota in patients with Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG), exploring their cross-sectional associations with nutritional intake.
papers.summary: This study compared the gut microbiota of ALS patients with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG), finding differences in microbial composition that may relate to nutritional intake. The results suggest that PEG feeding is associated with distinct gut microbiome profiles in ALS patients, potentially relevant for disease management.

papers.title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis and functional alterations in Campylobacter-associated gastroenteritis using metagenomic approaches.
papers.abstract: Campylobacter species are a major cause of bacterial gastroenteritis worldwide. Using shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from PCR-confirmed Campylobacter-positive patients and symptomatic PCR-negative controls, we reveal dysbiosis marked by reduced species richness (median Shannon diversity was significantly lower in the Campylobacter-positive group [3.24] vs. Campylobacter-negative group [3.63], P = 0.038), taxonomic shifts toward inflammation-associated taxa (Campylobacteriaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, Pasteurellaceae), and depletion of key commensals involved in short-chain fatty
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize gut microbiome dysbiosis in Campylobacter-associated gastroenteritis, finding reduced species diversity and shifts toward inflammation-associated taxa while depleting beneficial commensals involved in short-chain fatty acid production.

papers.title: Bioinformatic tools for microbiome analysis: from raw sequences to biological insights.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of microbiome research has been accompanied by an expanding but fragmented ecosystem of bioinformatic tools. Researchers now face a daunting array of software packages, pipelines, and web platforms spanning every stage of analysis, from quality control and taxonomic profiling to functional annotation and statistical interpretation. While this diversity offers flexibility, it also creates challenges in selecting appropriate tools and integrating them into coherent, reproducible workflows, particularly for researchers without formal computational training. This review presents a
papers.summary: This review provides an overview of the fragmented bioinformatics tool ecosystem for microbiome analysis, covering stages from raw sequence processing to biological interpretation. It highlights the challenges researchers face in selecting and integrating tools into reproducible workflows, especially for those without computational expertise.

papers.title: Decoding the rhizosphere microbiome against Sclerotium rolfsii: integrating multi-omics and AI-driven predictive models.
papers.abstract: The soil-borne necrotrophic fungus Sclerotium rolfsii is a globally important pathogen causing collar rot, southern blight, and damping-off in diverse crops, resulting in substantial losses in yield, particularly during warm and cloudy weather. Through processes like niche competition, antibiosis, induced systemic resistance, and enzymatic destruction of pathogen propagules, there is mounting evidence that the rhizosphere microbiome is crucial in influencing disease outcomes. This systemic review synthesizes published evidence on rhizosphere microbial structure and function under S. rolfsii pr
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on how the rhizosphere microbiome influences disease outcomes against the soil-borne pathogen Sclerotium rolfsii, highlighting mechanisms such as niche competition, antibiosis, induced systemic resistance, and enzymatic degradation. It advocates for integrating multi-omics approaches with AI-driven predictive models to decode microbiome-plant-pathogen interactions and develop sustainable disease management strategies.

papers.title: Gut microbiota of sprint athletes: signature microbes and dietary links.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota has emerged as an important biological factor associated with host physiological status in athletes. However, relevant research remains limited for sprint athletes, whose physiological demands differ substantially from those of endurance athletes.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the gut microbiota of sprint athletes, identifying signature microbes and their associations with dietary patterns, which differ from those seen in endurance athletes. The findings highlight unique microbial features linked to the physiological demands of sprinting, suggesting potential targets for performance-related interventions.

papers.title: Gut microbiota-derived imidazole propionate is associated with obesity.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a progressive metabolic disorder with some well-recognized markers, such as increased or elevated branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs). However, the role of gut microbiota-derived metabolites remains unknown in Asian populations. By employing an integrated multi-omics approach combining metagenomic and plasma metabolomic profiling in an Asian cohort alongside a longitudinal analysis of a bariatric surgery subgroup. We identified a distinct metabolic signature in obesity characterized by depleted circulating histidine and a concomitant elevation of Imidazole Propionate (ImP). The eleva
papers.summary: This study identifies a distinct metabolic signature in an Asian cohort with obesity, characterized by depleted circulating histidine and elevated gut microbiota-derived imidazole propionate (ImP). Using integrated metagenomic and metabolomic profiling, the authors show that ImP levels are associated with obesity and change after bariatric surgery, suggesting a potential role for this microbial metabolite in obesity pathogenesis.

papers.title: Ecosystem settings and urbanization shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance genes on coastal microplastics.
papers.abstract: Coastal wetlands are increasingly contaminated by microplastics that provide long-lived substrates for microbial colonization, yet the joint effects of ecosystem settings and urbanization on plastisphere communities and their resistomes remain poorly understood. Here, we used a 2 × 2 factorial design across mangrove and sandy-beach sediments under rural and urban influence, combined with metagenomic profiling, to characterize microplastic-associated microbiota and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Microbial communities on microplastics showed clear separation between mangroves and sandy shor
papers.summary: This study used a factorial design across mangrove and sandy-beach sediments under rural and urban influence, combined with metagenomic profiling, to show that both ecosystem type and urbanization level shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance genes on coastal microplastics. The findings reveal that plastisphere communities and their resistomes are distinct between mangroves and sandy shores, with urbanization further influencing their composition.

papers.title: From natural assemblages to synthetic communities in the Lupinus microbiome.
papers.abstract: Plant roots harbour complex microbial communities that enhance nutrient acquisition, stress tolerance, and pathogen defence, yet their assembly and functional dynamics remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the Lupinus (lupin) root microbiome, highlighting how natural microbial assemblages contribute to plant health and how synthetic microbial communities can be designed to replicate these functions. It emphasizes the need to understand assembly rules and functional interactions to translate microbiome insights into agricultural applications.

papers.title: Application-focused validation of a viability-selective PMA-qPCR assay for selected skin-associated and cosmetic-relevant bacteria.
papers.abstract: Accurate quantification of viable bacteria is essential for ensuring product safety and quality in the food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetics industries. However, conventional plate culture methods are time-consuming and fail to detect viable but non-culturable (VBNC) cells, which frequently occur under environmental stress or preservation conditions and can influence product stability and safety. Accordingly, the need for a quantification method that accounts for VBNC cells has increased. In this study, we optimized and validated a viability-selective quantification method by combining propidium
papers.summary: This study optimized and validated a PMA-qPCR method for selectively quantifying viable bacteria relevant to skin and cosmetics, addressing the limitations of plate culture in detecting viable but non-culturable (VBNC) cells. The method provides a faster, more accurate alternative for product safety and quality testing in the cosmetics industry.

papers.title: Characterization of the intestinal microbial profile in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) are major contributors to dementia, with growing prevalence in Latin America. Evidence suggests that gut microbiota alterations may influence neurodegeneration, but data on Hispanic population are lacking.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the gut microbiome in patients with mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on a Hispanic population where such data were previously lacking. It likely identifies microbial signatures associated with cognitive decline, providing insights into the gut-brain axis in this understudied group.

papers.title: Differential gut microbiota modulation associated with anti-Parkinsonian effects of Ophiopogon japonicus across geographical origins and extraction methods.
papers.abstract: Ophiopogon japonicus (OJ) is a medicine-food homologous plant widely consumed in East Asia and has attracted attention for its potential anti-Parkinsonian properties. However, the influence of geographical origin and extraction methods on its bioactive profile, gut microbiota modulation, and anti-Parkinsonian effects remain insufficiently understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the geographical origin and extraction method of Ophiopogon japonicus (OJ) affect its anti-Parkinsonian effects, focusing on gut microbiota modulation. The findings reveal that different OJ preparations differentially alter the gut microbiome, which correlates with varying neuroprotective benefits, highlighting the importance of standardization for therapeutic use.

papers.title: Microbial colonisation of the neonatal beef calf gastrointestinal tract: limited influence of birth delivery method across five anatomical regions.
papers.abstract: The microbiome assembly of the neonatal gastrointestinal tract is critical for immune and metabolic development, and birth delivery method can influence initial microbial colonisation. Using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, we investigated the effect of transvaginal and elective caesarean section delivery on microbial composition across five gastrointestinal regions (colon, ileum, jejunum, meconium, and rumen) in Aberdeen Angus calves (transvaginal, TV; n = 12; caesarean section, CS; n = 10) across two research farms. Absolute microbial quantities were measured using 16S rRNA qPCR. Alpha div
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and qPCR to compare the gastrointestinal microbiome of neonatal beef calves delivered vaginally versus by caesarean section across five gut regions. The authors found that birth delivery method had only a limited influence on microbial colonisation, suggesting other factors may play a larger role in early microbiome assembly in calves.

papers.title: Assessment of gut microbiota dynamics and probiotic impact on HPV-associated head and neck cancer using 16S rRNA sequencing and cytokine profiling.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major etiological factor in head and neck cancers, primarily through the oncogenic activities of viral proteins E6 and E7, which disrupt the p53 and retinoblastoma (Rb) tumor suppressor pathways. This disruption promotes uncontrolled cell proliferation, immune dysregulation, chronic inflammation, and malignant transformation. Although probiotics have emerged as promising modulators of the microbiome and host immune responses, their mechanistic role in HPV-associated head and neck cancer remains insufficiently understood. Therefore, this study investigated the th
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study examines gut microbiota dynamics and the impact of probiotics in HPV-associated head and neck cancer using 16S rRNA sequencing and cytokine profiling. The findings suggest that probiotics may modulate the gut microbiome and immune responses, potentially offering a supportive role in managing this cancer type.

papers.title: Preoperative gut microbiota combined with machine learning for predicting post-hepatectomy liver failure in HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the association between preoperative gut microbiota (GM) profiles and post-hepatectomy liver failure (PHLF) in patients with newly diagnosed HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC), aiming to explore non-invasive, modifiable GM biomarkers for perioperative risk stratification.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This pilot study explores whether preoperative gut microbiota profiles can predict post-hepatectomy liver failure in patients with HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma, using machine learning. The findings suggest that specific gut microbial signatures combined with clinical data may offer a non-invasive approach for perioperative risk stratification, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Genetic predictive links between oropharyngeal microecology and obstructive sleep apnea syndrome: expanding the perspective of etiology.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS), a global public health concern, is linked to oropharyngeal microbiota, but observational studies cannot confirm their causal association.
papers.summary: This study uses genetic data to investigate whether oropharyngeal microbiota composition is causally linked to obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS), moving beyond observational correlations. The findings suggest potential causal relationships between specific microbes and OSAS risk, offering new insights into the disease's etiology.
